(ABATED SINCE DIED) (By Sri.B.J.M., Advocate) JUDGMENT The petitioners have filed the petition under Section 12 of Protection of Woman from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against the respondents. 
2. The case of the petitioners in brief is as under:
a. The petitioner No.1 is the legally wedded wife of respondent No.1. Their marriage took place on 12.10.2008 at Sri Gayathri Temple, Yeshwanthpura Circle,
Yeshwanthpura, Bengaluru, in the presence of relatives and friends from both Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT families, following Hindu rites and customs. A female child was born from their wedlock. After their marriage, the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.1 initially lived happily in the matrimonial home. However, the respondents soon began to find fault with petitioner No.1 over trivial matters. No matter what the petitioner No.1 did, respondents No.1 and 2 constantly blamed her Anitha. B.S vs Ganesan R on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152473508/
1 for every household task. They began treating petitioner No.1 as a maidservant,
forcing her to do all the household chores without rest, which caused her considerable mental and physical distress. 
b. The petitioners' states that, during marriage discussions, Respondents Nos. 1 and 2 demanded Rs. 2 Lakhs in cash as well as gold ornaments, silver items, steel vessels,
and clothing for both Petitioner No. 1 and the Respondents. 
Petitioner No. 1's parents agreed to these demands, providing Rs. 2 Lakhs in cash as dowry. The gold items provided included one necklace, a pair of bangles, nine earrings, three rings, and a chain for Petitioner No. 1, along with a gold chain and a ring for Respondent No. 1, totalling 152.11 grams. Petitioner No. 1's Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT parents also provided various silver items,
including a silver plate, chambu, panchapatra, uddhane, Lakshminarayana vigraha,
Krishna vigraha, deepa, Kubera deepa, panchavala, a silver bowl, Ganesha vigraha,
agarbatti stand, leg chains, and two kumkum cups, valued at Rs. 49,300. In addition,
steel items provided included a Prestige cooker, a 12-piece plate and cup set,
koladappale set, spoon set, steel boxes, sout, large dabari, steel mug, chambu, oil can,
coffee dabari with handle, tappale, masala box set, steel basin, coffee glass and dabari, palya battalu, steel dabari set, ghee bowl, large spoons, maguchi kai, brass lamp, fancy bowl set, fancy lamp, Radhakrishna vigraha, and Srirama photo, totaling approximately Rs. 20,000/-. Furthermore, the clothing provided included 12 silk sarees, 15 shirt pieces, 15 pant pieces, one dhare dhoti, one silk maguta, and two ordinary dhotis, totaling Rs. 60,900/-. 
c. Petitioner No.1 states that the first month of marriage was harmonious, but after that, respondents No.1 and Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT 2 began criticizing her over insignificant issues. Regardless of her efforts, the respondents continued to berate her for everything she did around the house. As petitioner No.1 was newly married and adjusting to a new environment, she initially did not take their abusive words seriously. However, as she tolerated the mistreatment, the respondents took advantage of her silence and escalated their harassment. The respondents also began verbally degrading petitioner No.1 and her parents. 
They never showed concern for her wellbeing, including not allowing her to have a proper meal. 
Petitioner No.1 was only permitted to eat whatever food remained after the respondents had finished their dinner.
d. Furthermore, respondents No.1 and 2 demanded that petitioner No.1 find a job, stating that they would not provide her with any financial support unless she earned her own income and handed over her entire salary to them. In order to appease them and with the hope of leading a happier married life, petitioner No.1 secured employment on 01.06.2009 at Vidya Ratna P.T.S Matriculation Higher Secondary School, Crl. Misc . No.147/2012 JUDGMENT Adyar, Chennai, with a monthly salary of Rs. 3,000/- . From the very first month, the petitioner was forced to hand over her entire Anitha. B.S vs Ganesan R on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152473508/
2 salary to respondents No.1 and 2, keeping nothing for herself. Despite her contributions, the respondents did not provide her with any financial assistance or meet her basic needs, resulting in both economic and emotional abuse. This situation caused severe mental and physical distress to petitioner No.1.
e. The petitioner No.1 submits that on 04/10/2009, at around 11 PM, respondent No.1 assaulted her when she expressed her desire to visit her parents in Bangalore. Enraged by her request, respondent No.1 physically attacked her, striking her all over her body. He attempted to throttle her and caused a leg injury by standing on her feet. He even tried to kill her. Due to the unbearable pain, petitioner No.1 screamed, and upon hearing her cries, respondent No.1 stopped the assault and left the room. 
Respondent No.2, aware of the assault, did nothing to intervene. Instead, with the intent to support respondent No.1, respondent No.2 indirectly encouraged the Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT abuse by failing to rescue petitioner No.1. As a result of the assault, petitioner No.1 suffered injuries all over her body, as well as pain in her neck and feet. The respondents prevented her from seeking medical treatment, forcing petitioner No.1 to rely on painkillers at home to manage the pain. 
f. Again, on 31/10/2009, at approximately 8 to 8:30 PM, when petitioner No.1 came to the room to sleep, respondent No.1 physically assaulted her again. This time, it was because she refused to ask her father to buy a new car for respondent No.1. He grabbed her by the hair, forced her veil into her mouth to silence her screams, and sat on her while beating her severely. The assault left petitioner No.1 with bruises and caused her immense pain in her stomach and throughout her body. When petitioner No.1 was on the verge of losing consciousness, respondent No.1 left the room, leaving her in that state. This incident caused petitioner No.1 extreme physical pain and instilled fear in her mind, as she realized that respondent No.1 was capable of killing her. The petitioner also suffered mentally due to the violent behaviour of respondent Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT No.1,
instigated by respondent No.2. Despite the severity of these assaults, petitioner No.1 did not disclose the incidents to anyone, hoping to save her marriage and believing that respondent No.1 might change his behaviour in the future. 
g. The petitioner No.1 submits that she has been subjected to sexual abuse by respondent No.1. His conduct was both humiliating and degrading, causing petitioner No.1 to lose her dignity as a traditional woman. She endured the sexual abuse to avoid further mistreatment from respondents No.1 and 2. Due to the lack of proper nutrition provided by the respondents, petitioner No.1 often felt unwell and experienced pain throughout her body. Unable to bear the pain any longer, she requested permission from respondents No.1 and 2 to see a doctor. After much persuasion, they reluctantly agreed, and petitioner No.1 visited a hospital in Adyar. There, she was examined by Dr.
Hemachandrika, a civil surgeon at Tamil Nadu Medical Service Hospital, on 11/01/2010. The doctor also conducted a pregnancy test and informed petitioner No.1 that she was pregnant. However,
petitioner No.1 was physically and Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT mentally weakened due to the various acts of violence inflicted upon her by respondents No.1 and 2. 
Anitha. B.S vs Ganesan R on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152473508/
3 h. The petitioner No.1 further submits that upon learning of her pregnancy, she hoped that respondents No.1 and 2 would change their violent behavior and stop the assaults. She decided to inform respondent No.1 about the pregnancy on the night of 11/01/2010. However, to her shock,
respondent No.1 told her that he did not want a child and demanded that she abort the pregnancy. 
He further threatened her, stating that if she did not comply, he would physically assault her until she miscarried. When petitioner No.1 refused to abort the child, respondent No.2 also verbally abused her in filthy language, saying that "the petitioner is like a dog and should obey whatever we command." Respondent No.2 further insulted petitioner No.1 by saying, "We mistakenly married this dog to our son; otherwise, we could have gotten a daughter-in- law from a wealthy family in our community." Additionally, respondent No.2 insulted petitioner No.1's father, stating, "Your Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT father is an idiot and not on our level; we made a mistake allowing him to tie you to our family like a burden."
i. The petitioner No.1 submits that on 03/09/2010, she gave birth to a female baby named Keerthi Shravani, who is now nearly 2 years old. After the child's birth, petitioner No.1's parents informed the respondents by letter on 06/09/2010, but the respondents did not bother to respond, as they were displeased with the birth of a female child. Following the delivery, petitioner No.1 wrote a letter to respondent No.1 on 06/09/2010, requesting him to perform the customary rituals. After learning of her discharge from the hospital, respondent No.1 visited petitioner No.1's parents' house on 07/09/2010. When respondent No.1 arrived at about 5:00 PM, petitioner No.1's parents welcomed him with snacks. Despite her optimism that respondent No.1 might change his behavior after the birth of the baby, petitioner No.1 was shocked when, in the presence of her friend H.S. Rathna Kumari and her parents, respondent No.1 verbally abused her. He stated that he did not want a baby in his house, especially not a female child. He Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT further threatened that he would never allow her to join him in Adyar and that if she did so against his wishes, he would kill both her and the child. He even told petitioner No.1 to hang herself in Bangalore and not return to him. 
j. This public humiliation caused petitioner No.1 immense pain, especially since respondent No.1 openly insulted her in front of her friend and family members. Respondent No.1 did not even look at their child, petitioner No.2, and on the same day, he returned to Adyar. Since that day, neither respondent No.1 nor respondent No.2 has visited petitioner No.1, nor have they called her to return to her matrimonial home. 
k. The petitioner submits that from 13/07/2011, she stayed with her child in her matrimonial home,
but all her hopes were in vain as respondents No.1 and 2 did not stop their habitual assaults and violence. Instead, their abusive behavior worsened day by day, making her life feel like imprisonment. The respondents restricted petitioner No.1's movements and did Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT not allow her to leave the house. Every day, they would drag her,
lock her inside a room, and leave her confined. Petitioner No.1 and her child were not provided with sufficient food, which caused immense suffering. The respondents threatened to kill both her and her child if she informed anyone about the abuse. Petitioner No.1 was forced to do all the household chores without being allowed to properly care for her child. After completing her work, respondent No.2 would confine both petitioner No.1 and her child in a room, preventing her from moving freely Anitha. B.S vs Ganesan R on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152473508/
4 around the house or visiting other parts of the residence. This routine of physical assault, verbal abuse, and emotional torment became a daily ordeal for petitioner No.1, with the intent of coercing her into leaving the matrimonial home. 
l. In the second week of August 2011, petitioner No.2 fell ill with a fever, but the respondents showed no concern. They neither took the child to the hospital nor allowed petitioner No.1 to do so. Despite her child's illness, the respondents continued their physical torture, causing injuries Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT and endangering her health. They also verbally abused her in filthy language, further harassing her mentally. The respondents' actions were aimed at forcing petitioner No.1 to leave, as they were displeased with having a female child and were unhappy with petitioner No.1's financial background, since her parents did not meet their illegal demands. 
m. The petitioner No.1 submits that, unable to bear the physical and mental torture inflicted by respondents No.1 and 2, she informed her parents by telephone on 01/09/2011 that her health,
safety, life, and that of her daughter, Keerthi, were in danger. She expressed fear for their lives and requested her father's help. Shocked by the situation, petitioner No.1's parents immediately decided to rescue their daughter and granddaughter. On 07/09/2011, they arrived at Adyar, where respondents had locked petitioner No.1 and her child in a room and refused to let her parents enter the house or see them. 
n. In response, petitioner No.1's father rushed to the Adyar police station and reported the matter. 
The police Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT accompanied him to the house, where they found petitioner No.1 and her child illegally detained by the respondents in a locked room. After assessing the situation, the Adyar police released petitioner No.1 and her child and advised her parents to take them back to Bangalore, as their lives were clearly in danger. On the same day, 07/09/2011,
petitioner No.1's parents took her and her child to Bangalore to ensure their safety. Since then,
petitioner No.1 has been residing with her child at her parents' house. 
o. From 07/09/2011, petitioner No.1 has been living with her parents in their rented home. 
However, due to her parents' advanced age and the various ailments they suffer from, petitioner No.1 and her child have become a significant burden for them. If petitioner No.1 continues to stay with her parents, it will cause further hardship for the family. Meanwhile, respondent No.1 is employed as a manager at Indian Overseas Bank, earning a salary of Rs.60,000 per month. He also owns ancestral property in Chennai and Crl. Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT receives rental income of Rs.50,000 per month. Hence, petitioners prayed to allow the petition. 
3. After service of notice the respondents have appeared before the Court through their Counsel and filed objection denying entire case of the petitioner, except the relationship. 
a. The respondents submit that both Petitioner No. 1 and Respondent No. 1 have divorced their former spouses, and this is the second marriage for each of them. The respondents contend that Petitioner No. 1 frequently quarreled with the respondents and behaved arrogantly, bringing disrespect to them. During her pregnancy, Petitioner No. 1 allegedly threatened Respondent No. 1 in September 2009, stating she would commit suicide if not allowed to pursue a teaching position. 
Anitha. B.S vs Ganesan R on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152473508/
5 Subsequently, she was permitted to join the job, and her parents were informed of her behavior. 
b. The respondents further deny the allegations in paragraph 16, asserting that they are false and fabricated. They Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT claim that Petitioner No. 1 took two gold bangles weighing five sovereigns, which belonged to Respondent No. 2. They also contend that Petitioner No. 1 refused to visit Respondent No. 1 in Bangalore, asserting that she had strongly expressed her unwillingness to see him. Letters sent between the parties were, according to the respondents, formal and meant to cover up Petitioner No. 1's alleged faults. The respondents add that the petitioner's parents sent a letter on 6.9.2010 to inform them of the child's birth on 3.9.2010,
even though there were ample opportunities to inform them by phone or internet. The respondents argue that these documents were preplanned to support a false complaint, indicating ill intentions on the part of Petitioner No. 1 and her parents. 
c. The respondents also deny the allegations in paragraph 23, asserting no such incident occurred and denying any abuse by Respondent No. 1 in front of Mrs. Rathnakumari, whom they describe as a stranger to them. They claim that Petitioner No. 1 prevented Respondent No. 1 from seeing or accessing the child, threatened to commit suicide with the Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT child,
refused to participate in family festivals such as Varalakshmi Pooja and Ganesh Pooja, and filed a false complaint with the Adayar police station, which was ultimately dismissed. 
d. Additionally, the respondents state that Petitioner No. 1 left the matrimonial home, indicating she would return with the child within 15 days, yet she later filed for divorce in the Family Court at Bangalore. They claim that Petitioner No. 1 used a similar strategy to file a divorce petition against her first husband, making baseless allegations and securing a substantial financial settlement. The respondents allege she is attempting the same approach to extract money from Respondent No. 1.
e. The respondents assert that all allegations are false and beyond belief, urging the Court to dismiss the application. They argue that Petitioner No. 1 deserted Respondent No. 1 and has prevented him from seeing the child due to her "superiority complex" and financial independence. The respondents state that Respondent No. 1 is committed to the child's future and is Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT ready to support her education as needed. They also contend that the inclusion of Respondent No. 2, an elderly person, is intended solely to harass, and that this constitutes a misjoinder of parties.
f. The respondents argue that the complaint is based on false allegations and is an abuse of the legal process. Therefore, they pray that this Hon'ble Court dismiss the petition filed against them under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, as it lacks legal and moral merit. With these contentions, the respondents prayed to reject the petition. 
4. To substantiate their case, the petitioner No.1 testified as PW.1 and submitted documents marked as Ex. P.1 to P.93, after which she closed her side of the case. Ex. In defense, Respondent No.1 testified as RW.1 and submitted documents marked as Ex.R.1 to R.35, after which he closed his side of the case. Ex. P.92 and Ex . P.93 were confronted to RW.1 Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT during his cross-examination. During Anitha.B.S vs Ganesan R on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152473508/
6 the pendency of the proceedings, Respondent No. 2 was reported as died. 
5. I have heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material on record. 
6. The points that arise for my consideration are;
1. Whether the petitioners prove that petitioner No.1 has been subjected to cruelty of domestic violence and neglected by the respondents?
2. Whether the petitioners further prove that, the respondents having sufficient means and have deserted the petitioners? 
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for maintenance? 
4. What order? 
7. The findings of this Court on the above points are as under:
 Point No.1 : In the Negative;
 Point No.2 : In the Negative;
 Point No.3 : In the Negative;
 Point No.4 : As per final order for the  following:
 Crl.Misc.No.147/2012  JUDGMENT  REASONS 8. Points No.1 & 2 :Since these points are inter related to each other hence they have been taken together for discussion for the sake of convenience and to avoid repetition of the facts and evidence. 
9. It is specific case of the petitioner No.1 that, petitioner No.1 being legally wedded wife of respondent No.1 has been subjected to cruelty and domestic violence by the respondents. She contended that, her marriage was solemnized on 12.10.2008 at Sri Gayathri Temple,
Yeshwanthpura Circle, Yeshwanthpura, Bengaluru, as per Hindu rites and customs in the presence of relatives and friends of both the family members. Out of their wedlock, one female child was born to them. During the stay of petitioner No. in the house of respondents, the respondents have given ill-treatment to the petitioners and drove out the petitioners without providing any maintenance. 
Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT 10. The petitioners averred in the petition about the ill- treatment and domestic violence committed by the respondents and also deposed as PW-1 by reiterating the petition averments and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.93. 11. The respondents have appeared before the Court and filed objections denying the case of the petitioners. The respondents in order to establish their defense the respondent NO.1 got examined as RW-1 by filing affidavit evidence in lieu of his examination in chief, wherein he has deposed in consonance with the averments of the objection and in support of his oral evidence he has got marked Ex.R.1 to R.35. Ex.R.1 is Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT the Teachers Certificate, Ex.R.2 is the Annual Magazine from Sheshadripuram Pre-primary and Higher Primary School, Ex.R.3 to 12 are the Photos, Ex.R.13 is the Hotel Bill, Ex.R.14 & 15 are the Two Cash Bills, Ex.R.16 to 18 are the Tax Invoices, Ex.R.19 & 20 are the Two Photos, Ex.R.21 & 22 are the Certified copy of petition and examination-in-chief of petitioner in M.C.No.1087/1998, Ex.R.23 is the Certified copy of Judgment in M.C.No.1087/1998, Ex.R.24 is the Certified copy of memorandum of petition in M.F.A.No.681/2002, Ex.R.25 is the Pelvic Scan Report, Ex.R.26 & 27 are the Photos, Ex.R.28 is the Prescription, Ex.R.29 is the Photo, Ex.R.30 is the Legal Notice dated 13.10.2011, Ex.R.31 is the Certified copy of petition in M.C.No.4301/2011, Ex.R.32 & 33 are the Certified copy of FIR and complaint, Ex.R.34 is the Certified copy of written statement of the respondent and Ex.R.35 is the Copy of Index in M.C.No.4301/2011. 
12. The learned counsel for the petitioners argued that the petitioners have detailed several incidents of domestic Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT violence committed by the respondents. It was further argued that Respondent No. 1 failed to provide any financial support for the petitioner and their child, which constitutes economic abuse. The counsel emphasized that Respondent No. 1 only began providing monetary support following a court order. Based on these submissions, the counsel requested the court to allow the petition. 
13. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the respondents contended that the allegations of domestic violence were made against the respondents are false. The counsel further argued that no additional witnesses were presented to corroborate the petitioner's claims. It was also asserted that Anitha.B.S vs Ganesan R on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152473508/
8 the petitioner voluntarily left the matrimonial home and refused to return, despite Respondent No. 1 making multiple attempts to reconcile and settle the matter. With these submissions, the counsel urged the court to dismiss the petition. 
14. At the very outset, it is pertinent to mention that complainant in order to be entitled to the relief under the Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is required to establish,
that firstly there is a domestic relationship as defined under Section 2(f) of the abovesaid Act between complainant and respondents and thereafter it is also required to be established that she has been a victim of domestic violence as defined under Section 3 of the said Act. Domestic relationship has been defined under the Act in Section 2(f) as under:
(f)"domestic relationship" means a relationship between two persons who live or have, at any point of time, lived together in a shared household, when they are related by consanguinity, marriage, or through a relationship in the nature of marriage, adoption or are family members living together as a joint family. 
15. It is observed that the fact of the marriage between the petitioner No.1 and Respondent No. 1 is not disputed by either party. This is further substantiated through documentary evidence marked as Ex.P.1, which is marriage card. It is also undisputed that Keerthi Shravani was born from this union. 
Therefore, the domestic relationship between the petitioner No.1 and Respondent No.1 is established. 
Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT 16. The petitioners contend that, during the marriage discussions, Respondents Nos. 1 and 2 demanded Rs. 2 Lakhs in cash, along with gold ornaments, silver items, steel vessels, and clothing for both Petitioner No. 1 and the Respondents. Petitioner No. 1's parents agreed to these demands and provided Rs. 2 Lakhs in cash as dowry. The gold items given included one necklace, a pair of bangles, nine earrings, three rings, and a chain for Petitioner No. 1, as well as a gold chain and a ring for Respondent No. 1, with a total weight of 152.11 grams. Petitioner No. 1's parents also provided various silver items, such as a silver plate, chambu, panchapatra, uddhane, Lakshminarayana vigraha, Krishna vigraha, deepa, Kubera deepa, panchavala, a silver bowl, Ganesha vigraha,
agarbatti stand, leg chains, and two kumkum cups, with a total value of Rs. 49,300.
17. In addition, steel items were provided, including a Prestige cooker, a 12-piece plate and cup set,
koladappale set, spoon set, steel boxes, sout, large dabari, steel mug, chambu, Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT oil can, coffee dabari with handle, tappale, masala box set, steel basin, coffee glass and dabari, palya battalu, steel dabari set, ghee bowl, large spoons, maguchi kai, brass lamp, fancy bowl set, fancy lamp, Radhakrishna vigraha, and Srirama photo, totaling approximately Rs. 20,000. 
Furthermore, clothing items included 12 silk sarees, 15 shirt pieces, 15 pant pieces, one dhare dhoti,
one silk maguta, and two ordinary dhotis, totalling Rs. 60,900.
18. On 12.07.2024, the counsel for the Respondents filed a memo accompanied by a certified copy of the Judgment delivered by the Hon'ble 24th Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate of Bengaluru,
Anitha.B.S vs Ganesan R on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152473508/
9 in Criminal Case No. 8633/2012, dated 06.04.2024. Although this judgment is not specifically referenced in the order sheet, it forms part of the official case file. Upon examination of this Judgment, it is evident that the Hon'ble 24th ACMM Court acquitted the Respondents of the charges under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act. 
Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT 19. Section 498A of the IPC pertains to the offense of subjecting a married woman to cruelty, which includes both physical and mental harassment, especially in relation to dowry demands. Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act address the giving, taking, or abetting of dowry, outlining the prohibition of any demand for dowry before, during, or after marriage. The court, after examining the evidence presented, found it insufficient to establish that the Respondents had committed acts of cruelty or made illegal demands for dowry as alleged by the petitioners. 
20. The petitioners have not contested or refuted this acquittal order in their submissions, which further strengthens its standing. The Hon'ble 24th ACMM Court's ruling, by dismissing the allegations of cruelty and dowry demand, effectively negates the claims put forward by Petitioner No. 1 regarding dowry and related harassment. The acquittal, therefore, serves as a critical factor,
casting significant doubt on the validity of the petitioners' allegations, as it reflects the court's determination that the charges were unsubstantiated. 
Crl.Misc.No.147/2012 JUDGMENT 21. In view of this acquittal, the allegations of dowry demands and cruelty raised by Petitioner No. 1 cannot be upheld, as the Hon'ble 24th ACMM Court found no basis for a conviction on those charges. Consequently, this judgment considerably weakens the position of the petitioners by undermining the legal foundation of their claims related to dowry and cruelty. 
22.
